modulus<i32>

radix/corpus/operatores/modular-word-signed.fab (canonical · operator-group)#

Signed wrapping integers: the ring of 2^W values with signed representatives, as in a Java hash.

# =============================================================================
# 模數<i32> — Signed wrapping integers: the ring of 2^W values with signed representatives.
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • Signed ring — `wrapping<i8>` holds -128..127 and wraps at both ends:
#     127 + 1 is -128, and `-128 / -1` is -128 again.
#   • Floor division — `/` and `%` floor on the representatives: -7 / 2 is -4
#     and -7 % 2 is 1.
#   • Arithmetic shift and complement — `⇒` keeps the sign (-8 ⇒ 1 is -4) and
#     `¬` is the complement inside the ring (¬-8 is 7).
#   • Reduction on entry — `↦ wrapping<i8>` and a constant stored with `←`
#     reduce into the ring: 300 becomes 44, and 200 becomes -56.
#   • A real port — Java's `String.hashCode` is `h = 31 * h + c` over a signed
#     32-bit word; "hello" hashes to 99162322.
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • Expecting a trap on overflow — `wrapping` reduces, it never traps. Only a
#     zero divisor fails.
#   • Mixing families — `wrapping<i8> + i8` is an error; convert with `↦`.
#
# See also: 整數, 模數, ¬, ⇒
# =============================================================================

fn javaHash(list<int> codes) → wrapping<i32> {
    var wrapping<i32> h ← 0
    for from codes const c {
        const wrapping<i32> code ← c ↦ wrapping<i32>
        h ← 31 * h + code
    }
    return h
}

main {
    var wrapping<i8> a ← 127
    a ← a + 1
    print a
    const wrapping<i8> m ← -128
    const wrapping<i8> quotient ← m / -1
    print quotient
    const wrapping<i8> n ← -7
    print n / 2
    print n % 2
    const wrapping<i8> s ← -8
    print s ⇒ 1
    print ¬s
    const int wide ← 300
    print wide ↦ wrapping<i8>
    const int over ← 200
    print over ↦ wrapping<i8>
    const wrapping<i8> c ← 200
    print c
    print javaHash([104, 101, 108, 108, 111])
}

Expected output:

-128
-128
-4
1
-4
7
44
-56
-56
99162322
